article.headline: California Chemical Tank Crack Sparks State of Emergency, Thousands Evacuated
article.summary: A chemical tank at an aerospace plant in Garden Grove, California, has cracked, prompting a state of emergency and the evacuation of 50,000 residents. The tank, which holds 7,000 gallons of the highly toxic and flammable chemical methyl methacrylate, is at risk of leaking or exploding. Emergency responders are working to mitigate the situation, with firefighters continuously spraying the tank with water to keep it cool.
article.body:
The incident began on Thursday when the chemicals in the tank began to exceed a safe temperature, causing concerns about a potential explosion. By Friday, residents in the surrounding area were ordered to evacuate as a precautionary measure. The chemical, methyl methacrylate, is used in the manufacturing of resins and plastics and can cause skin and eye irritation, respiratory issues, and neurological symptoms.

The tank, located at the GKN Aerospace facility, has been damaged and was bulging outward before the crack was discovered. Firefighters have been spraying the tank with water to keep it cool, and one of the adjacent tanks has been safely drained and neutralized. The incident commander, Craig Covey, stated that if the damaged tank were to crack, it could actually be the best outcome, as it would allow the chemical to leak out slowly rather than sparking an explosion inside the tank.

The company that owns the plant, GKN Aerospace, has said that it is working around the clock to mitigate the risk of a leak. The Orange County Fire Authority has set up containment barriers and laid down sand and other materials to try and stem the flow of the chemical into nearby storm drains and waterways. The Environmental Protection Agency has also set up monitoring stations around the site to detect any potential fumes.

Despite the efforts to contain the situation, residents are still being advised to remain evacuated until it is deemed safe to return. The fire department is unable to predict which way any potential fumes might travel, and as a result, a large area around the plant has been evacuated. So far, no fumes have been detected, but the situation remains volatile.

The incident has sparked concerns about the potential environmental and health impacts of a chemical spill. Methyl methacrylate can cause long-term damage to lungs and organs, and the environmental impacts of a spill are still unknown. The Orange County Fire Authority is working to minimize the risks and ensure the safety of the surrounding community.
article.takeaway: The cracked chemical tank in California has sparked a state of emergency, with thousands evacuated and emergency responders working to mitigate the risk of a leak or explosion, highlighting the potential dangers of industrial accidents involving highly toxic and flammable chemicals.
